title: Rabbah bar Itai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places Rabbah bar Itai in Rav’s time and refers to his entry on Rava bar Itai. For [Sotah 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.30a.3) he also proposes “Rabbah bar Itai said in the name of Rabbah,” adding that this requires further investigation.

notes.text: The received Sotah text gives Rav Asi speaking in Rav’s name, with Rabbah ben Isi as an alternative transmitter of the same teaching. Hyman’s proposed Rabbah bar Itai reading remains tentative.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3091&lang=en) compares the Rava bar Itai readings in [Shevuot 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.37a.4) and [Bava Metzia 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.14a.6) with Rabbah bar Itai in the Hebrew of [Keritot 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.24a.13). The English of the latter link reads Rava.

In Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1071), the preceding notice about Rabbah bar Isi ends “and perhaps he is,” immediately before the heading Rabbah bar Itai. In the consulted Sotah 30a, Rav Asi reports Rav’s teaching, with Rabbah ben Isi named as the alternate reporter. Hyman’s cross-entry (p. 1058) gives “Rava (or Rabbah) bar Itai.” The consulted Shevuot 37a and Bava Metzia 14a read Rava, and the Hebrew of Keritot 24a reads Rabbah where the English has Rava. The identification and the proposed reading in Sotah remain tentative.
